classification_rules.consistent: bbox IoU >= 0.70 AND keypoint px diff <= 2.0 (<=0.72 deg) AND present/visibility/reference_status semantics match
classification_rules.acceptable_deviation: (0.30 <= IoU < 0.70) OR (2.0 < keypoint diff <= 4.0 px, i.e. 0.72-1.43 deg), with semantics matching
classification_rules.substantive_disagreement: IoU < 0.30 OR keypoint diff > 4.0 px OR any semantic mismatch in present/visibility/reference_status/negative_type
classification_rules.undeterminable: reference point unavailable on either side (no keypoint comparison possible) OR target identity flagged ambiguous OR one side has no bbox on a present target

threshold_justification.iou_0.70: two independent annotators of the same object normally exceed 0.7 when the bbox extent convention agrees; lower IoU indicates extent-convention or boundary disagreement
threshold_justification.iou_0.30: the proposed downstream bbox-assist threshold (configs/perception/geometry_test_freeze_v2.json / labels v2 iou_threshold_proposed), below which the box is not usable as the same object
threshold_justification.keypoint_2px: 0.5x the 4-8 px green-light core width, i.e. a plausible independent-annotator centre difference
threshold_justification.keypoint_4px: >=1x green-light core width and ~1.4 deg; beyond a defensible manual centre difference; note this is still below the proposed 5 deg bearing gate (=~14 px), so it matters for annotation consistency, not necessarily for downstream bearing acceptance

sensitivity_check: a pure colour-cue centroid (mask: g>=90, g-r>=25, g-b>=25, 4-connectivity, >=2 px) is computed for every present frame as an independent reference-point estimator; old labels are reported against BOTH the visual blind pick and the colour-cue centroid
note: these thresholds are PROPOSED for this verification only; they are not competition metrics and not a frozen acceptance gate
